# New package

Packages come from the generator, never by hand. Rules: [Code structure](../../engineering.md#code-structure), [Ownership boundary](../../engineering.md#ownership-boundary), [Public API and stability](../../engineering.md#public-api-and-stability). Reasoning: ADRs [0006](../../../docs/adr/0006-seams-go-down.md) (seams go down), [0007](../../../docs/adr/0007-entry-vocabulary.md) (entries), [0008](../../../docs/adr/0008-placement-and-dependencies.md) (placement), [0009](../../../docs/adr/0009-generated-workspace-shape.md) (generated shape), and [0010](../../../docs/adr/0010-test-versus-runtime-ownership.md) (test versus runtime).

## 1. Confirm a package is the answer

Find the [concern owner](../../../docs/architecture.md#concern-owners) first; enhancing it usually beats a new package. A technology integration never becomes a core subpath; use [new-backend](../new-backend/SKILL.md) to choose its owner. Dev-only tooling goes in `internal/` through `bun run gen tool`. Test machinery consumers use ships in `testkit` or `mocks`.

## 2. Name and place it

- One plain word for one concern, used everywhere. Check the npm name is free: `npm view @plainworks/<name>`.
- Pick the lowest layer in the [layer map](../../../docs/architecture.md#layer-map) that holds everything it imports. If it needs something higher, the seam belongs lower.

## 3. Generate it

```bash
bun run gen package --args <name> "<one-line description>" <hasClient>
bun install
```

`hasClient` is `true` only when the package ships React bindings; it adds a DOM-free `./client` with per-module `"use client"`, a jsdom test project, and catalog React peers. Declare `dom: true` only when the product is browser UI. New public subpaths go in `build.entry` in `tsdown.config.ts`, followed by `bun run sync-shape`; never hand-edit derived manifest fields.

## 4. Join the layer map

Until it is in [`layers.json`](../../../internal/boundaries/layers.json), the boundary gate forbids any `@plainworks` import (it fails closed). Add it at its layer, run `bun run sync-layer-map`, and extend the boundaries fixture test when the new relationship needs coverage.

## 5. Build test-first

Follow [apply-step](../apply-step/SKILL.md). Start with concern-named modules and a re-export-only `src/index.ts`. Reuse `std` and `testkit` owners. Security-critical packages raise their coverage floor. Client code meets [UI quality](../../engineering.md#ui-quality) and composes atoms from `@plainworks/elements/<name>`, never copying or editing them.

Write the README for a first-time consumer: concern, import, runnable example, then entries and errors. Every public export gets TSDoc.

## 6. Validate

```bash
bun run check-shape
bun run verify --filter=@plainworks/<name>
bun run changeset
```

Use the [validate](../validate/SKILL.md) skill for UI or integration proof.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Generated by `bun run gen package`; `check-shape` green; no hand-edited derived fields
- [ ] One plain concern name; placed in `layers.json` and the layer map synced
- [ ] Imports only lower layers; neutral `.` free of React, DOM, and Node
- [ ] Small typed public surface with TSDoc; README leads with a runnable example
- [ ] Tests written first; client code accessible and responsive
- [ ] `bun run verify --filter=@plainworks/<name>` green and a Changeset added

Edit only; commits and pushes need the user's authorization.
